scope: Child-friendly named-taxon-inspired static environment prop, 80–240 px and moderate 480 px inspection; no strict scientific reconstruction or publication decision.

criteria.evidence: Validator: zero errors/warnings. Source/export comparison: 2064 triangles and bounds match exactly; reproducible GLB bytes and semantic digest match. 103448 bytes, 4 materials, 8 primitives, 0 textures meet budgets. Free-swimming mount explains negative minimum Y. Smooth body is intentional and visually clean.

All source and exact-export fixed views inspected. At 80/160/240 px, deep forebody, taper, dorsal fin and forked tail remain readable; at 480 px no conspicuous detached major component, penetration or broken shading. End-on tail/median-fin collapse is expected foreshortening.

Side, hero, reversehero and silhouette show elongate herring-like body, deeper anterior half and narrow caudal peduncle; does not read as a deep oval armored fish. DIP-WY Physical Characteristics supports deep-bodied form; DIP-NPS Fish Wall identifies freshwater herring.

Side and hero at 240/480 px show a small dark seam rising to a raised snout; front shows both seam halves meeting at the upper tip. Dorsal edge has a restrained small scute rhythm and no head shield. DIP-WY explicitly supports upturned mouth; exact scute count/shape is an artistic simplification, not a verified specimen claim.

Source/browser side, front, top and bottom show one dorsal, one anal, paired pectoral/pelvic fins, and a deeply notched two-lobed tail. Gray view preserves secondary structure. Visible joins seat into the body with no floating major parts. Fin panels are deliberately stylized and have visible edge thickness. No exact fin-ray formula claimed. Repaired tessellation removes the caudal notch overlap; new exact-export views retain clean thickness and joins.

Editable source, standalone GLB, deterministic generator/config, required QA views and hero poster exist with stylized/static labels. Final freeze.json is the versioned execution-brief supplement; all six source/generator/config/brief/reference/GLB SHA-256 values and byte lengths independently verified against actual files.
Final browser/diplomystus.json binds exact GLB hash to Three.js r180 GLTFLoader, matching bounds, 4 materials/8 primitives/0 textures, no errors or failed requests.

Seven browser export views plus three projected-size views inspected. Final WebGL2 report passes with ANGLE Vulkan SwiftShader. Functional software rendering only; no physical GPU performance claim. Initial favicon-only 404 report is superseded.

Scene hero/top pixels inspected: three fish copies among nine props are visible. Final scene report passes, 76 calls and 31214 submitted triangles including floor. Final scene loaded entry and isolated report both bind the exact fish hash. Neutral benchmark only, no museum/coexistence or hardware throughput claim.

advisories: Mouth/scute/ray details naturally reduce or disappear at 80 px; core fish identity and tail fork survive.
Planar ochre fin panels and smooth blue body are coherent stylization; raised fin rays are decorative simplification.
Museum page text was read directly; museum specimen image download returned 403, so exact fin/scute morphology was not independently established from that image.

warnings_disposition.smooth_body: Intentional calm body surface; source clay and browser views show no unexplained creases.
warnings_disposition.below_ground: Documented free-swimming centerline origin; no floor-contact requirement.

references_read.location: Physical Characteristics; body form/upturned mouth and general preserved fins

revision_recheck.change: Concave sheet faces use tessellate_polygon instead of center fan; outline preserved.
revision_recheck.observed_outcome: Forked caudal notch clean in source hero/reversehero/side/clay and browser matching views; full required-view and 80/160/240/480 px regression check passed. No further revision requested.
